# Sort Integers by Binary Reflection.

@example The reflections are 13, 5, 9 and 1: 11 is 1011, which reads 1101 backwards, and 10 is 1010, which reads 0101.
[11,10,9,16]
=> [16,10,9,11]

@example 2 reflects to 1 and 7 to 7; 3, 12 and 24 all reflect to 3, so they come between, smallest first.
[12,24,7,3,2]
=> [2,3,12,24,7]

@example 5 and 20 (10100) both reflect to 5; both copies of 20 are kept.
[20,5,20,1]
=> [1,5,20,20]

# A single element.
[37]
=> [37]

# Powers of two all reflect to 1, so they lead, smallest first, even when
# listed largest first.
[536870912,64,3,1024,1]
=> [1,64,1024,536870912,3]

# One family listed from largest to smallest, and a second one mixed in:
# keeping the input order within a reflection is wrong.
[80,40,48,5,24,3]
=> [3,24,48,5,40,80]

# 1-bit, 3-bit and 30-bit values together: the bits are reversed over each
# number's own length, not over 32 (or 30) bits. 6 is 110, so it reflects
# to 3.
[536870913,7,6,5,1]
=> [1,6,5,7,536870913]

# 805306367 is 10 followed by 28 ones: its reflection is 2^30 - 3, above
# 10^9. 999999999 reflects to 1071961719 and 10^9 to 1365623.
[805306367,1000000000,999999999,1]
=> [1,1000000000,999999999,805306367]

# 10^9 is 1953125 times 2^9, so the two share a reflection, 1365623, and
# the smaller comes first. 976562500 is 244140625 times 4, another family,
# whose reflection is 145042199.
[1000000000,976562500,1953125]
=> [1953125,1000000000,976562500]

# Numbers whose bits read the same both ways reflect to themselves.
[21,17,15,9]
=> [9,15,17,21]

# All equal.
[100,100,100]
=> [100,100,100]

# Duplicates in two families.
[3,1,3,2,1]
=> [1,1,2,3,3]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[2,6,8,21,112,86989500,670902084]
=> [2,8,6,112,21,86989500,670902084]

@gen 2 small
[8,18,11,3,20]
=> [8,3,20,18,11]

@gen 3 small
[112,52,36,26,25,11,8,2]
=> [2,8,112,36,26,52,11,25]

@gen 4 small
[11,22,4,37]
=> [4,11,22,37]

@gen 5 small
[22,22,44,80,240,165482840]
=> [80,22,22,44,240,165482840]

@gen 6 small
[547062979,20]
=> [20,547062979]
